Separate label-1-cycle recurrence and exact harmonic-base recalculation
correctness.rationale: Conditioning on one designated fixed point adds a singleton to a uniform permutation of n−1 and increases its second length precisely in the one-cycle case, which has probability 1/(n−1). Since E[F_n]=1, this gives the covariance identity. Uniform insertion uses m existing arrows and the singleton option. Insertion at an existing arrow increases the second-ranked length only when a strictly larger cycle already exists and the chosen arrow is in a second-ranked cycle. Thus the arrow contribution is B_m C_{B_m} with the stated strict-rank indicator, giving (1−T_m)/(m+1). The disjoint cycle types (a,b) and (a,b,1) with the stated restrictions each contribute 1/a. Their harmonic sum has strictly positive two-step difference in each parity by comparing its four positive fractions with the smallest fraction, and the bases 841/840 and 6527/6435 exceed one. I recomputed those bases and the full finite boundary table by a separate exact recurrence: condition on the length j of the cycle containing label 1, uniform on 1 through n, insert j into the top-two length pair of the remainder, and update the fixed-point-weighted mass by adding ordinary mass if j=1. It reproduced all ten entries, including +1/30 at 5 and −1/36 at 6; the harmonic argument covers the rest. For the limit, one can avoid any small-second-cycle estimate: pointwise the absolute difference of the insertion statistic and B_m is bounded by the sum of j C_j(C_j−1) over j. Counting pairs of disjoint labelled cycles gives E[C_j(C_j−1)]=1/j² for 2j≤m and zero otherwise. The resulting O(log m) error suffices, with Shepp–Lloyd's mean limit, to get −γ₂. The original long-cycle tie proof is also valid.
residual_risks: The finite recurrence checks the boundary cases, not future sizes. The limit uses the classical ranked-cycle mean and applies only to uniform permutations with the stated tie conventions.

evidence: Shepp–Lloyd give limiting moments at general ranks and the exact displayed decimal for the second-ranked mean fraction. Ford bounds long-length multiplicities. The two covariance records 7a0ec035875d and 700d4371e2f3 condition on a longest-cycle cutoff or on exactly three cycles, respectively.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General marginal ranked-cycle laws and cycle-count bounds furnish ingredients. Unlike the frozen claim, the nearby covariance records are conditioned models with different statistics; setting the Ewens parameter to one does not remove their conditioning or change a cycle count into a ranked length.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the all-size dependence classification: the sign is positive through n=5 and strictly negative at every n≥6. The ranked-cycle insertion recurrence and the value of γ₂ are classical. The covariance identity is an elementary fixed-point marking reduction, and the asymptotic covariance is a short consequence of that reduction, classical ranked-cycle ingredients and tie control. Neither alone is the basis for passing originality. The inspected prior passages and related catalogue statements do not give the decisive finite sign boundary with permanence.
residual_risks: The primary comparison was targeted, not a broad historical search. The capped index queries and passage comparisons cannot exclude an earlier unlocated exact inequality or covariance identity.

value.rationale: An all-size sign boundary for a natural local statistic and a macroscopic rank gives information unavailable from marginal moments. The proof identifies the precise finite crossover and excludes later reversals or zeros, which is stronger than a numerical observation or a limiting negative covariance. The harmonic argument makes the cutoff uniform, rather than a cutoff chosen for computational convenience.
residual_risks: The scientific value is the sharp sign law for the stated pair. It does not establish an all-ranks or all-Ewens-parameter analogue.
